newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea sells dollars at 895 won - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea sells dollars at 895 won - dealers.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea was seen intervening in the interbank foreign exchange market on Monday by selling dollars at 895 won, dealers said.
The bank then intervened two more times, selling dollars in one-month forward trading at 898.50 won and in six-month forward trading at 916.00 won, they said.
The dollar fell to 894.50 won at 0140 GMT in spot after the intervention. It opened at 894.60 and rose to 895.00.
A central bank official earlier said the bank wants the dollar to weaken against the local currency and indicated its firm intention to stabilise the won/dollar rate.
"We want the dollar to move below the 895 won level," the official said. "Without changes in economic fundamentals, there is no doubt the dollar would weaken (versus the local currency)."
He said the central bank, concerned about the economy, would "aggressively react" to any speculative dollar buying.
